title: Ray diagrams
examples: How do I know if a lens is converging or diverging?
Can you show me how to draw the image for a concave mirror?
What does the position of the image tell me about the lens?

explain.say: Today we are learning about ray diagrams for lenses. These diagrams help us see where light rays go. We will learn about two types of lenses. One is called a converging lens. Another type is a diverging lens. You need to know how to draw these diagrams correctly.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a convex lens. Look at the convex lens, the object and the focal point. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

A converging lens, also called a convex lens, bends parallel light rays inward. These rays meet at a point called the focal point. Think of it like a magnifying glass. It gathers all the light in one spot.

A diverging lens, or a concave lens, spreads out parallel light rays. It makes the light rays appear to come from a point further away. It never actually focuses the light to a single point. It always spreads it out.

When drawing a ray diagram, the image can be real or virtual. A real image forms where actual light rays actually meet. A virtual image appears to come from where rays seem to diverge from. You need to check this carefully.

Consider a converging lens with an object placed at two times the focal length. The image formed will be real, inverted, and located at two focal lengths on the other side. This is a common setup to practice with.
In everyday life, magnifying glasses use converging lenses. They help us see small objects much larger. This allows us to see details on leaves or insects clearly. It is a very useful optical tool.

faq.q: What is the difference between a real and a virtual image?
faq.a: A real image is formed where actual light rays converge. A virtual image is formed where light rays only appear to diverge from.
asks: How do I tell if an image is real?
What does 'virtual' mean for an image?

faq.q: Does the lens type change how the image forms?
faq.a: Yes, converging lenses focus light, while diverging lenses spread light out. This changes the location and nature of the image.
asks: Do I use the same diagram for both lenses?
What happens if I use a concave lens?

faq.q: What does the focal length mean for a lens?
faq.a: The focal length is the distance from the lens to the focal point. It is a key measurement for drawing the diagram.
asks: Is focal length the same as radius?
How do I find the focal length?

faq.q: Do I need to draw the principal axis?
faq.a: Yes, you must always draw the principal axis. This is the straight line passing through the optical centre of the lens.
asks: Where do I draw the main line?

faq.q: If the object is far away, where is the image?
faq.a: For a converging lens, if the object is far away, the image will be formed close to the focal point. This is a key rule to remember.
asks: What happens when object distance is infinity?
Where does the image go if the object is very far?

facts: Converging lenses bend parallel light rays towards the principal axis.
Diverging lenses spread out parallel light rays away from the principal axis.
A real image can be projected onto a screen. A virtual image cannot.
The focal length is the distance to the focal point for the lens.

quiz.say: Which type of lens bends parallel light rays inward to a focus?
quiz.why: Converging lenses, or convex lenses, are defined by their ability to gather light rays to a focus point.

wrong.0: Diverging lenses always spread light out; they do not focus it.
wrong.1: This is a mirror, not a lens, and its reflection properties are different.
wrong.2: Plane glass has no optical effect on light rays passing through it.

quiz.say: If an object is placed just outside the focal point of a converging lens, where is the image formed?
quiz.why: When the object is placed near the focal point, the image forms on the opposite side and is magnified.

wrong.0: Placing the object exactly at the focal point causes the rays to be parallel, forming an image at infinity.
wrong.1: The image position depends on the lens and object distance, not just matching the object.
wrong.2: The image formed by a converging lens with a real object is always real and on the opposite side.

quiz.say: When drawing a diagram, if the light rays only seem to come from a point, what kind of image is it?
quiz.why: A virtual image is one that is formed by the apparent intersection of light rays.

wrong.1: A real image means the light actually passes through that point.
wrong.2: This term describes the location, not the nature, of the image.
wrong.3: Inverted describes the orientation, not whether the image is real or virtual.
